confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.28 (EC-10): "RUN_OPENING(ref) := ref.space === 'C9' ∧ c9Registry.get(ref.key).mode ∈ {'PROPOSE_ONLY', 'OWNER_HANDOFF'}", carrying the normative sentence "PR2 (a′), normative. The emission validator refuses any intent whose `subjectCapability(i)` satisfies `RUN_OPENING` on an envelope whose `origin` is `PROACTIVE`."
confirmedFindings.justification: The finding survives on the contract's own stated bar. §0C.11-bis declares, verbatim, "the two accessors this section names are declared here … A normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares, so both are declared", and the code block it then gives declares exactly two: `c9Registry.tryGet = (key: string) => C9_CAP_BY_KEY.get(key);` and `actionCapabilityRegistry.tryGet`. `c9Registry.get` is declared by no shape in the contract and by nothing in the repository: a literal grep over all 5 881 lines yields four `c9Registry` occurrences — 1363, 1478 and 1616 all `tryGet`, and 2009 alone `get` — and `grep -rn "c9Registry" src/` in maya-saas-backend returns zero, so the object exists only as this contract's own declaration with a single member. Nothing cures it: §0C.13's EC-10 row is what *installs* `RUN_OPENING` ("Replaced by `RUN_OPENING(ref)` over the existing `mode` member (15 of 56)"), §0.16 and §0B.9 are silent, §0C.28 carries no `*Status:*` line (unlike S0C.7, S0C.11-bis, S0C.15, S0C.17, S0C.26, EC-11's ruling, all of which do), §0C.12's non-normative register does not list PR2, and §0.17 lists neither PR2 nor §4.9.2 among the downgraded items. This is precisely the class the contract itself adjudicates as structural twice in this very section — EC-6 voided a clause for naming `a11y.accessible_name`, "a carrier … that `A11yBlock` does not declare", and EC-15 is titled "the two remaining dangling identifiers" and declares `body_hash` and `selection_domain` even though their host prerequisite P-30 is `[ABSENT]`, so pendency of the emission validator is no excuse. The second half of the finding also holds: every sibling C9 lookup in 0-C is written `c9Registry.tryGet(...)?.…` with an explicit FAIL-CLOSED branch (`c9Floor`: "if (cap === undefined) return 'STEP_UP_VERIFIED'; // FAIL CLOSED — unregistered"; `C9_MODE_FLOOR`/`C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR`: "default: return 'STEP_UP_VERIFIED'; // FAIL-CLOSED DEFAULT"; `FLOOR_EXEMPT` at line 1616), whereas §0C.28 dereferences `.mode` off an unguarded lookup — so bound to the one declared accessor it yields `undefined ∉ {PROPOSE_ONLY, OWNER_HANDOFF}` ⟹ RUN_OPENING false ⟹ the proactive envelope is admitted, the refusing polarity inverted, and bound to `c9Capability` it is the throwing run-admission function §0C.11-bis expressly forbids substituting ("Using it in a floor derivation would reproduce EC-2's defect exactly"). The repository facts §0C.28 rests on are otherwise correct and were re-verified in process — `C9_CAPABILITIES` = 56 with READ 41 / PROPOSE_ONLY 13 / OWNER_HANDOFF 2, i.e. 15 non-READ — so the defect is confined to the accessor and the missing unregistered-key case, and it does not lower a floor, admit a capability, widen an allowlist or relax a veto in the EC-10 repair's intent; it simply leaves PR2's replacement mechanism unconstructible as written.

confirmedFindings.justification: The clause survives every exemption and the repository facts are the filer's, not the contract's. EC-11 is not void (it is the ruling row of §0C.13, "Amended"), is not in §0C.12's non-normative register, and its `NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-01, P-26` marking excuses "not yet built", not "not constructible" — the contract itself applies exactly that distinction to a pending clause when §0C.22-bis says "A CI check over an identifier no shape declares is the very defect EC-6 exists to close, reproduced in its own repair", and when EC-15 declares `body_hash`/`selection_domain` for the equally-pending Gate 8-R. `domain` is a required positional `C9Domain` argument (`c9.registry.ts:178-192`: `if (!def || !def.domains.includes(domain) || (domain === 'BUSINESS_INTELLIGENCE' && def.mode !== 'READ')) c9Deny(...)`), and §0C.11-bis names that dependency itself — c9Capability "additionally demands a `C9Domain` argument … would make the floor depend on which domain is asking". A full-text scan of all 5 881 lines finds exactly one domain-valued member in the whole contract, `Correlation.agent_id: 'ADMIN'|'CLIENT_LIFECYCLE'|'OCCUPANCY'|'BUSINESS_INTELLIGENCE'|null` (§1.1.4, line 2389) — envelope-level, nullable, and named by no gate; §3.7's `IntentRecord` as extended by §0C.26-ter and EC-15 declares no domain member, `CapabilityRef` is `{space,key}` (§0B.7), and `run_ref` is null on the capability-read mint path §1.1.4 declares ("`run_id` is nullable because two paths mint envelopes"), which is the path these nine take. Executed in process against the repo (baselines confirmed: C9 56, catalogue 47, AE 226), the free variable is outcome-determining rather than cosmetic: passing `def.domains[0]` admits all nine (the domain test is vacuous and the BI/non-READ clause never fires, since no non-READ key among the nine has BI first), `'BUSINESS_INTELLIGENCE'` refuses `b35.preview`, `b35.status`, `b35.confirm`, `a22.configuration`, `'ADMIN'` refuses five others, and `null` refuses all 56. §0C.32's EC-2 disclosure row nevertheless names this branch as one of the three things that "still fences these nine" after EC-2 lowers eight to SESSION_VERIFIED and `c9.no_action` to ANONYMOUS — so the one compensating fence added by this round cannot be written as specified, and every way of writing it either withdraws the fence or refuses an arbitrary subset. The defect is fail-closed in the worst case (a null domain refuses everything), so it is not a security-contract violation, but it is squarely the structural class: a normative clause of the highest-precedence section whose evaluation depends on an identifier no shape in the contract declares at its stated evaluation point, EP-INGRESS Gate 6.

confirmedFindings.justification: The clause survives every escape. (1) The member is undeclared. `c9Registry` is not a repository object at all — executing the registry gives `exports C9_CAPABILITIES,C9_REGISTRY_HASH,c9Capability,c9Available` (56 rows; mode READ 41 / PROPOSE_ONLY 13 / OWNER_HANDOFF 2, so the filer's 15-of-56 claim is exactly right). `c9Registry` therefore exists only as declared by the contract, and the contract declares it in exactly one place, §0C.11-bis line 1478: "c9Registry.tryGet = (key: string) => C9_CAP_BY_KEY.get(key);" — introduced by the ruling that "A normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares, so both are declared, and the reason neither existing accessor can do the work is stated rather than left to a reader", and closing with "the two that already exist may not be substituted for them". `.get` appears on `c9Registry` exactly once in 5,881 lines (line 2009); lines 1363, 1478 and 1616 all use `.tryGet`. (2) It is normative, not illustrative: the block is immediately consumed by "> **PR2 (a′), normative.** The emission validator refuses any intent whose `subjectCapability(i)` satisfies `RUN_OPENING` … *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`." (3) No errata row covers it. 0C.13's EC-10 row *is* this repair and cites §0C.28 approvingly; EC-15, which exists precisely to close "the two remaining dangling identifiers", names only `body_hash` and `selection_domain`; nothing in 0.16, 0B.9 or 0C.13 voids or amends §0C.28, and no NORMATIVE-PENDING or [NON-NORMATIVE] marking attaches to the block. (4) Both charitable readings fail, so it is not a harmless typo. Read as `c9Capability`, §0C.11-bis forbids the substitution in terms: it "**throws** `c9Deny('capability_not_registered')`, additionally demands a `C9Domain` argument, and refuses on a registry-hash mismatch … Using it in a floor derivation would reproduce EC-2's defect exactly" — verified against `c9.registry.ts:178–192`, which takes `(key, domain: C9Domain, registryHash)` and calls `c9Deny` on miss; RUN_OPENING supplies neither a domain nor a hash, so the predicate is not even arity-compatible. Read as `tryGet`, the return is `C9Capability | undefined` and `.mode` is an access on possibly-undefined, making a predicate the emission validator must evaluate on every C9-space intent partial — and the contract itself proves unregistered C9 keys are reachable, since §0C.10's sibling `c9Floor` guards exactly that case ("if (cap === undefined) return 'STEP_UP_VERIFIED'; // FAIL CLOSED — unregistered"). This is the recurrence of the class §0C.22-bis (line 1797) names in its own repair. It does not lower a floor, admit a capability or relax a veto — it is a structural defect, not a security one.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22 (EC-6), A-2 as amended: "*Mechanism:* a CI check over each emitted `A11yBlock` asserting, for every `ref ∈ a11y.reading_order`, that `a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(intentOf(ref).label)`" — together with "In every case the accessible name contains `intent.label` as a prefix, by construction" and §0C.22-bis's "`keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order)` at `EP-MINT`, and an envelope whose `reading_order` names a ref with no entry is refused."
confirmedFindings.justification: The finding survives every exemption and every counter-reading I could construct. (1) `intentOf` occurs exactly once in the whole 5,881-line artefact — at line 1788, inside A-2's own mechanism — and no shape, function table or errata row declares it; §0.16, §0B.9 and §0C.13 were checked row by row, and EC-15 ("the two remaining dangling identifiers") declares only `IntentRecord.body_hash` and `selection_domain`. (2) It cannot be made total over its stated domain: §4.8 types `reading_order: InteractiveRef[]` and `InteractiveRef` includes `| { k: 'field'; id: string }  // FormField.field_key`; §2.6.17 declares FORM's "**Interactive paths** `fields[].field_key`, `submit_intent`, `discard_intent`, `editor_handoff_intent`" and §2 K22 requires `reading_order` to "contain exactly the refs produced by `KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths`", so every FORM envelope's `reading_order` carries up to twelve `{k:'field'}` refs; a `FormField` is not a `WidgetIntent` and carries `label: LocaleText`, never `intent.label`. §0C.22-bis then forces an `accessible_names` entry for each of those refs on pain of refusal, and A-2 demands each such entry begin with a member that does not exist. (3) The `NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-19 / P-31` marking does not cure it, by this section's own doctrine: §0C.21 rejects exactly that defence — "§A2.8's `NORMATIVE-PENDING` marking repairs only the status half — a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have." (4) Nor does the "§4.8.2 is the sole per-kind normative owner" sentence: §4.8.2's FORM row exists, so A-2's prefix clause applies rather than being displaced, and FORM is listed Emittable in §2.7. This is the identical defect class EC-6 exists to close — §0C.21 voids the original A-2 because "`WidgetIntent` declares no member `utterance`" so "the named CI string check cannot be written" — reproduced in the repair, which is precisely the recurrence round 5 was told to look for. The filer's consequence is marginally overstated (§0C.22-bis's `EP-MINT` rule is satisfiable for a FORM; what actually fails is A-2's `EP-BUILD` CI check, which then refuses rather than admits, so no build ships) but that does not touch the defect: a normative mechanism names an undeclared function and asserts a universal ("by construction") that is false for one of the sixteen kinds emittable today. Fail-closed throughout, so correctly filed as structural and not security.
confirmedFindings.repair: Two edits inside §0C.22, nothing else. (A) Declare the map, beside §0C.22-bis's `accessible_names` declaration: `function intentOf(ref: InteractiveRef, env: WidgetEnvelope): WidgetIntent | null` — for `{k:'intent'}` the envelope intent whose `intent_ref === ref.id`; for `{k:'option'|'row'|'entry'}` the single envelope-level intent whose `InputSchema` field of kind `enum`/`ref` carries `ref.id` in its closed `domain_ref` (the mapping §0.29 already fixes), else `null`; for `{k:'field'}` and `{k:'section'}` **`null` by definition**. Total over `InteractiveRef`, non-throwing. (B) Make A-2 conditional on it: where `intentOf(ref) !== null` the accessible name is `intent.label` + `', '` + the §4.8.2 row's composition (and `intent.label` verbatim where §4.8.2 supplies no row), and the CI assertion is `a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(intentOf(ref)!.label)`, quantified over `{ref ∈ reading_order : intentOf(ref) !== null}` only; where `intentOf(ref) === null` the accessible name is the §4.8.2 row's composition applied to that element alone — for a `FORM` field, its own `label`, `help`, `current` and `bound.basis` (§2.6.17) — and the `startsWith` assertion does not apply to it. Narrow the universal sentence to "In every case **where `intentOf(ref)` is non-null**, the accessible name contains `intent.label` as a prefix, by construction." `keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order)` is unchanged and stays total, so no floor is lowered and no ref loses its name.
